title: Hybrid credit-based preemptor with soft KV-quotas for workload fairness
creator: Aisha Mehta
description:
Problem: As we scale continuous batching across multi-tenant workloads, long-running KV-heavy requests and large-context generations monopolize GPU memory and batch slots, causing unfair latency regressions for latency-sensitive tenants. Existing hard-preempt/panic-evict approaches hurt tail quality and cause cache churn.

Goal: Design a hybrid preemption policy that is SLO-aware and prioritizes workload fairness while minimizing KV cache thrash and GPU memory compaction costs. The policy should: (1) allow cooperative yielding when possible, (2) provide per-tenant soft KV reservations to reduce painful cache eviction, (3) fall back to controlled hard preemption only when SLOs are at risk, and (4) provide clear observability and tunable knobs.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement cross-node global rebalancing or per-request model re-quantization. We assume single-GPU serving for the initial rollout and will expand to multi-GPU in a follow-up ticket.

High-level approach: Introduce a credit-based cooperative preemptor that accrues "yield credits" for queued/short-SLO requests over time. Concurrent KV-heavy requests hold a configurable soft quota of KV slab memory (soft KV reservations) that reduces eviction probability but can be voluntarily released. When a high-priority/low-latency request arrives and credits exceed a threshold, the scheduler first attempts cooperative yielding: it signals in-flight batches to checkpoint (flush partial KV state if safe), release soft quotas, or compact their KV slab. If cooperative actions achieve required free memory and batching slot targets within a latency budget, the incoming request proceeds without hard preemption. Otherwise, an ordered, SLO-aware hard preempt is executed with metrics-driven selection to minimize cache loss (prefer preempting the request with lowest effective cache-utility score).

Key components to implement:
- Credit accrual manager: per-tenant and per-route credits that increase while waiting and decay on usage; credits drive cooperative preempt suggestions.
- Soft KV reservations: small per-tenant soft quotas (configurable percentage of KV slab) with TTL and voluntary release hooks. Soft reservations reduce eviction probability but are reclaimable.
- Cooperative yield hooks in runtime: lightweight checkpoints, KV compaction triggers (non-blocking), and adaptive batch resizing to free transient tokens.
- Hard preempt selector: score requests by (remaining work, cache-utility, SLO headroom, tenant priority) and evict in an order that minimizes p99 regressions.
- GPU slab compaction pathway: background compaction that can be accelerated on demand when cooperative yield fails; must be bounded to avoid causing other SLO violations.

Metrics & SLOs to monitor: p50/p95/p99 latency per-route, queue wait time, batch fill rate, KV cache hit rate, KV eviction count, GPU memory fragmentation, preemption count (cooperative vs hard), user-facing error rate.

Acceptance criteria (see list): ensure no p99 SLO regressions for latency-sensitive routes during mixed workload experiments, and reduce KV eviction churn by at least 30% vs current baseline.
acceptance_criteria: No more than 5% relative increase in p99 for latency-sensitive routes during synthetic mixed-load tests
KV eviction count reduced by >=30% on mixed KV+latency workloads compared to baseline trunk with hard evictions
Cooperative yields succeed for at least 60% of soft-preemption cases in lab runs
Preemption telemetry (cooperative vs hard) exposed in Console per-route and per-tenant
Feature flag rollout path exists (off, conservative, permissive) with safe defaults
design_notes: Credit model: exponential backoff for accrual; fast decay on usage so credits reflect recent fairness pressure
Soft KV reservation size default: 6% of KV slab per tenant, configurable via tenant profile and route labels
Cooperative yield API: runtime exposes yield() hook that returns (released_bytes, compaction_time_estimate). If released_bytes meets request budget, scheduler proceeds.
Hard preempt ordering: score = alpha*cache_utility + beta*(1/SLO_headroom) + gamma*tenant_priority. Tune alpha/beta/gamma via A/B experiments.
GPU compaction: implement incremental slab compaction that runs for <=50ms per invocation and yields control back to serving runtime; full compacts are forbidden in the hot path.

Observability: add counters and histograms for credit accrual, soft-reservation totals, cooperative yield successes, and per-eviction cost estimate. Surface in Console and add alert when hard preempt ratio > 10% over 10m.
Backwards compatibility: default behavior when soft reservations disabled should revert to current preemptor to avoid regressions.
experiments: Lab harness: mixed synthetic workload (30% long-KV generations, 50% short-latency requests, 20% mid-length) with traffic shadowing to measure tail behavior
A/B rollout: 10% traffic (per-region) with conservative credit thresholds, compare p99, KV-eviction, and throughput vs control
Stress test: fill KV slab to 95% and inject burst low-latency requests to exercise hard fallback code paths
Memory footprint profiling: measure GPU fragmentation before/after cooperative compaction on M40-like and A100-like racks
implementation_plan: Step 1: implement credit manager and soft KV reservation metadata (runtime + control plane config)
Step 2: wire cooperative yield hooks in continuous batcher and add simple compaction routine
Step 3: implement hard preempt selector using scoring function and safe eviction path
Step 4: add telemetry and Console dashboard prototypes
Step 5: run lab experiments, tune alpha/beta/gamma, and cut canary release behind feature flag
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Cooperative yield may not release sufficient memory in time -> mitigation: conservative time budget and immediate fallback to hard preempt
Risk: Soft reservations might unfairly advantage noisy tenants -> mitigation: per-tenant cap and dynamic shrink when global pressure > threshold
Risk: Additional runtime complexity causing regressions -> mitigation: feature flag, thorough unit/integration tests, and staged rollout
Risk: Increased KV cache fragmentation after many voluntary releases -> mitigation: periodic background compaction and heuristics that prefer releasing low-utility keys
